title: Tradeoff matrix: cumulative model onboarding brief (Jun 2026)
content:
Executive summary:

This note summarizes the cumulative bakeoff we ran across 7 candidate model variants during the May–June onboarding sprint. Goal was to quantify tradeoffs across quality (task utility + instruction-following), latency (p95 token generation), and unit cost (estimated $/1k tokens under our serving profile). Unlike previous narrow head-to-heads, this run intentionally stacked 3 workload families (customer-support, code-editing hints, and knowledge-grounding chat) and a small adversarial prompt set to expose regressions.

High-level conclusion:
- No single candidate dominates on all axes. Two promising winners by use-case: Cobalt-v1 (best latency/cost for high-throughput embeddings/chat approximate tasks) and Cobalt-v2-deep (best utility for instruction-following & code tasks but higher latency/cost).
- Recommended short-term onboarding path: promote Cobalt-v1 to canary in Hosted API for default low-latency route (route: chat-low-latency), and run a 7-day A/B of Cobalt-v2-deep behind a dedicated model tag for codegen-heavy customers.

Background and motivation:
- Onboarding backlog had 7 candidate artifacts from model curation + 2 quantization variants (Q4 and Q8). We needed a single cross-workload analysis to guide routing policies (latency vs cost vs quality) and to surface any instruction-drift/regression risks before Dedicated commits.
- This doc captures the experimental setup, compact leaderboards, win/loss matrices, key failure modes, and an operational rollout checklist.

Methodology summary:
- Workloads: 3 canonical sets — support_short (2–3 turn support chats, n=1k prompts), code_suggest (docstring->implementation, n=800), grounded_search (long context retrieval QA, n=500). Adversarial set: edge_adversary (n=200).
- Metrics:
  - Utility: composite score = 0.6 * human QA + 0.4 * automated correctness (BLEU/ROUGE/semantic-similarity where applicable).
  - Latency: p50/p95 generation time measured under our batching simulation (10k simulated requests per model variant).
  - Cost: estimated $ per 1k tokens using hosted kernel profile + batching default (no KV cache) then adjusted for cache-hit scenarios.
  - Regression checks: instruction-following diffs vs baseline (Baseline = Cobalt-0.9-prod).
- Instrumentation: token-level tracing enabled, prompts salted with run-id, and evaluation forced deterministic seeds for sampling where needed.

Compact leaderboard (composite utility | latency p95 | est $/1k tokens | win-rate vs Baseline):
- Cobalt-v1-q8 | Utility 71.2 | Latency p95 42ms | $0.72/1k | Win-rate 58%
- Cobalt-v2-deep | Utility 78.9 | Latency p95 124ms | $1.85/1k | Win-rate 74%
- Cobalt-v2-deep-q4 | Utility 75.8 | Latency p95 98ms | $1.20/1k | Win-rate 66%
- Aegis-lite | Utility 68.4 | Latency p95 56ms | $0.95/1k | Win-rate 51%
- Aegis-pro | Utility 73.0 | Latency p95 140ms | $1.92/1k | Win-rate 61%
- Baseline (Cobalt-0.9-prod) | Utility 69.5 | Latency p95 60ms | $0.80/1k | Win-rate N/A
- Sparrow-slim | Utility 65.9 | Latency p95 35ms | $0.65/1k | Win-rate 39%

Notes on leaderboard interpretation:
- Utility is workload-weighted (support:40%, code:40%, grounded:20%). So improvements concentrated in code tasks drive big utility gains for Cobalt-v2-deep.
- Latency measured at our simulated 50rps per model node with continuous batching heuristics applied — real-world p95 will vary by dedicated capacity and cache-hit rates.

Win/loss quick matrix (ordered pairs against Baseline):
- Cobalt-v2-deep beat Baseline on code_suggest (win 82%), support_short (win 64%), tied on grounded_search (win 49%).
- Cobalt-v1-q8 traded quality for latency: lost on code_suggest (win 43%) but improved support_short (win 71%) and reduced token cost by ~10%.

Failure modes & triage highlights (top 6):
1) Instruction overreach: Cobalt-v2-deep occasionally hallucinated referenced code comments when ground truth absent (observed in 6% of code_suggest failures). Root cause: stronger prior for continuation, exacerbated by long context. Mitigation: prompt guardrails + conservative decoding during canary.
2) Verbose hedge in support_short: some variants (Aegis-pro) produced too-long apologies/hedging, increasing tokens and latency. Action: system prompt compression + token cap for support route.
3) Cost oscillation under burst: Q8 quantized variants saved cost at steady-state but under burst their batching collapses and p95 spikes. Operations to test under realistic burst patterns before Dedicated commits.
4) Retrieval-context trimming: grounded_search failures due to aggressive truncation of retrieved docs when pre-tokenization estimates were off. Fix: adopt our new token-estimator shim (PR linked).
5) Deterministic eval mismatch: small random seeds produced different BLEU ordering for close models — add more human evals for tie-breaks.
6) Safety filter false positives: Sparrow-slim triggered safety filter more often on code snippets flagged as "instructional", inflating failure rates.

Decision rationale and recommendations:
- Hosted API (default route): Promote Cobalt-v1-q8 into a 48-hour canary for chat-low-latency. Rationale: best latency/cost tradeoff for general-purpose low-latency needs, and wins on support_short workload which is representative of majority traffic. Canary thresholds: no >3% drop in top-level NPS proxy metric, p95 increase <= 15% on route, no new safety regression alerts.
- Hosted API (premium/code customers): A/B test Cobalt-v2-deep for identified customers with code-heavy usage. Run 7–14 day split with matched cohorts and extra human-eval sampling on code_suggest. If utility delta >6 points and cost delta acceptable (<2x), negotiate Dedicated commit/offers.
- Dedicated / Private: do not default to Cobalt-v2-deep for all Dedicated customers; recommend offering Cobalt-v2-deep as an opt-in model tag. Provide quantization/Q4 packaging as a cost-reduction option with clear latency impact notes.

Rollout checklist (operational):
- Create model tag: cobalt-v1-canary-0626 (Infra ticket INF-5621).
- Update routing policy: add cost-aware fallback to baseline if p95>2x for 5 consecutive minutes.
- Monitoring: activate per-route token-level histograms, setup regression alert if composite utility drops >3 points over 24h.
- Human eval sampling: 1% of canary requests flagged for human QA on code_suggest during first 72h.
- Docs & comms: draft release note for Public API changelog + send note to #applied-ml and #dev-rel.

Rollback criteria (immediate roll back to Baseline if any true):
- Safety breaches flagged by safety-team for new model (>=1 confirmed incident).
- Persistent latency p95 increase >50% for 30+ minutes during normal traffic.
- Composite utility drop >5 points sustained for 24h.

Open questions / unresolved items:
- Quantization parity: Q8 shows lower cost but regression on code tasks — need a small micro-benchmark to test whether further calibration (per-layer) reduces the utility delta (action: Marco to prototype per-layer q8 schedule, due 2026-06-25).
- Batch-utilization under multi-tenant load: performance model assumes isolated lanes — ops to simulate multi-tenant noisy neighbors.
- Customer communication: how to present opt-in model tags in the console without overwhelming non-technical users? Product to draft copy.

Appendix A — sample prompts used (representative):
- support_short example: "User: I can't download my invoice. System: [system prompt withheld]. User message: I need my invoice. What do I do?"
- code_suggest example: "Write a Python function that validates an email address using a single regex and returns True/False with tests."
- grounded_search example: "Given the attached docs, summarize the policy on data retention for marketing lists."

Appendix B — terse per-model notes and quick action items:
- Cobalt-v1-q8: low-risk canary. Action: enable for chat-low-latency, monitor token inflation.
- Cobalt-v2-deep: high-quality but high-cost. Action: run premium A/B and sample heavy-code buckets for manual review.
- Cobalt-v2-deep-q4: promising compromise; ops to test 2-node latency config.
- Aegis variants: stable on grounded_search but verbose on support_short. Prompt tuning recommended.
- Sparrow-slim: extremely cheap and low-latency but quality unacceptable for baseline replacement. Consider as microservice for embeddings-only flows.

Action items (owners):
- Aisha: create canary tag + open INF ticket for routing changes (due 2026-06-21).
- Marco: per-layer q8 prototype (due 2026-06-25).
- Liu: set up 7-day A/B experiment for Cobalt-v2-deep (experiment spec in linked_artifacts).
- Riley: draft customer-facing note and console copy (due 2026-06-22).

Notes to reviewers (quick): this is a working brief — please focus reviews on the rollout thresholds and whether the proposed A/B sampling is sufficient to detect codegen regressions. Slack thread: #applied-ml (see pinned "onboarding-run-0626").

---
Draft history: initial notes 2026-06-15 by Aisha; eval rerun for q4 quantization 2026-06-18 by Marco; human sample augmentation 2026-06-20 by Liu.

End of brief.
